transcript:
This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix into your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
In Alaska, Democrat Jonathan Christ Tompkins has won the race for governor according to a race called by the Associated Press.
As Eric Stone of Alaska Public Media reports, he'll replace the outgoing term-limited Republican Governor Mike Dunlavy.
Better known as J.K.T., Christ Tompkins spent a decade representing his hometown of Sitka as a state legislator after dropping out of Yale.
Now, at 37, he'll be the youngest governor in Alaska history and the first Democrat to lead the state since 2002.
Christ Tompkins says he ran on reaching across the aisle to solve problems that have bedeviled the state for years, from slow permitting to an underfunded school system.
We wanted to bring Alaskans together and focus on issues that unite more than they defied, and we want to be problem solvers.
He defeated three Republicans in the four-person ranked choice race, including one backed by President Trump.
For NPR News, I'm Eric Stone in Juneau, Alaska.
Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola has increased her lead in the race against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
The results of the additional balloting show the former Congresswoman, Peltola, now has 49.8 percent of the vote,
and under Alaska's ranked choice voting, if she reaches 50 percent, she'll be declared the winner.
Trump administration officials say no one was in danger, as the FAA called for a full ground stop for the first time since 9/11.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen briefed reporters at the White House after the ground stop was lifted.
The public was never at danger through this process. There was never any lives at risk.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also briefed reporters. He says the FAA switches got overloaded with data, became inconsistent,
and because of that, they shut the system down.
The secretary says Congress needs to fund a package that would help the FAA with new technology.
In the meantime, Duffy says a ground stop like this could happen again with the old technology in place.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, the White House.
European leaders gathered in Dublin, Ireland Friday. They agreed that Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and the U.K.
will send diplomats to talks with the U.S., Russia, and Ukraine.
Esme Nicholson reports.
Speaking after a summit focused on security and support for Ukraine, European Council President Antonio Costa
said five of Europe's major military powers will join EU institutions at the table in U.S.-led talks with Russia and Ukraine.
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner and Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky said Thursday that Europe would be part of the next round of talks.
European leaders are concerned that Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold sway over the Trump administration
to back a peace settlement that weakens Ukraine as well as Europe's security.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
And this is NPR News.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says additional military action against Iran is not necessary
because the economic pain that the U.S. military is inflicting on Iran is excessive.
And he said that victory is ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.
In a speech to the Federalist Society on Friday, Rubio acknowledged Americans are experiencing economic hardship as a result of the war,
which has driven up fuel costs. A tanker collided with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River at the port of New Orleans on Friday.
Eva Tesfaye of member station WWNO reports.
The American cruise line ship was docked for disembarking when the Atlantic asphalt container crashed into it, knocking it on its side.
Thirty passengers and two harbor police officers were taken to the hospital.
There are no critical injuries and all other passengers have been accounted for. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the response.
We are going to get down to the bottom of exactly what happened here
and make sure that we make any adjustments necessary so that the people that travel on the waterways here can know that they can do so in safety.
The Coast Guard is investigating the cause of the collision.
For NPR News, I'm Eva Tesfaye in New Orleans.
Republican Congresswoman Lauren Bobart of Colorado is the latest member of Congress to be defeated by a Democrat in the midterm elections.
Bobart was seeking a fourth term in the House.
Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Rear Admiral and a former member of the National Security Council during the Biden administration, defeated Bobart.
She is the third Colorado Democrat to win a Republican seat.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News.
Support for NPR.

Democrat Mary Peltola extends lead over Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska ranked-choice count
FAA halts all flights in first nationwide ground stop since 9/11 due to overloaded system
European leaders in Dublin agree Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and UK will join Ukraine-Russia talks
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says further military action against Iran unnecessary given economic pressure
